clue.text: The powers that be say I'm in the engineers

indicators.note: the clue places the example and the I'm inside the engineers, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
say signals an example, abbreviated EG
I'm gives the letters IM, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tells us the people in charge happen to be the military engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a speech verb but signals an example; RE stands for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is the ruling government or authority, the people holding power.

clue.text: About to open Plato's work

parts.note: re means about, concerning
public means open to all

explanation.surface: A Greek philosopher's writing is about to be launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'ready to', but 'About' is RE and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic is Plato's dialogue on justice and the ideal state.

clue.text: Reading out a description of leather

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word are disordered, thrown out of place

explanation.surface: Reading aloud a passage describing hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather with a visible pattern of the hide's surface is called grained.

clue.text: Show love in a public declaration

parts.note: to manifest is to show
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Displaying affection in a formal statement to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of policy or aims.

clue.text: Riverside fight setting a high tone

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall; 'side' tells us it sits beside the next piece
a set-to is a brief fight or scrap

explanation.surface: A brawl on a riverbank strikes a shrill, elevated note.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a Cornish river; 'setting' is only a link. 'Riverside' gives FAL, placed beside SET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high singing voice used by men above their natural range.

clue.text: In Berlin, so long as we feud in here, it'll be turbulent

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so the preceding words are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Germans quarrelling at length expect a stormy atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase is a farewell, goodbye until we meet again.

clue.text: Material's difficult to hear

annotationWithheld.why: Material's difficult to hear (5): STUFF needs S plus a sound of TOUGH, so 'Material's' is both the definition and the S

clue.text: Huge, and sort of acid

explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans; titanic acid is a compound of the element titanium.

clue.text: I ponder aloud, for no return

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: aloud signals that the thinking word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: to weigh something up is to ponder it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks out loud about never coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way ticket covers the outward trip only, with no journey back.

clue.text: Visitor's limits in Canadian city, below the station

indicators.note: below means in this down entry the city comes underneath the station

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
Regina is the capital of Saskatchewan

explanation.surface: A traveller's bounds are set by a Canadian town under the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'Visitor' are V and R, the royal cipher VR, short for Victoria Regina; Victoria is a London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: VR, the outer letters of the word, is the monogram standing for Queen Victoria's Latin title.

clue.text: Suitor with scheme to embrace one pet

indicators.note: to embrace means the scheme word wraps around the numeral one

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
one is the Roman numeral I
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff

explanation.surface: A wooer devises a plan to cuddle a favourite animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is not an animal but the old sense of a sulk, as in 'in a pet'; a tiff is a small quarrel. 'to embrace' puts I inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a suitor is one who brings a suit, i.e. the party who sues in court.

clue.text: Loose relative seen topless

indicators.note: topless means the relative's word loses its first letter

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: A wayward family member is spotted without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is a verb here, meaning set free; 'topless' drops the A from AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or a dog is to set it free, unfasten it.

clue.text: Advantage point after first of balls, if returned into net

indicators.note: after means the point follows the earlier piece
first of picks the opening letter of the word balls

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: into tells us the reversed word goes inside the net

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned means the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: A tennis scoring moment: a ball comes back into the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture of a ball coming back into the net misleads: 'Advantage' is the definition, not a score call.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage that something brings.

clue.text: Child presented to a princess

parts.note: a child is an infant

explanation.surface: A youngster is introduced to a royal lady.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch, a royal princess.

clue.text: River in South of France flowing backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: flowing backwards means the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: sud is French for south

explanation.surface: A river in the Midi runs the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' means south in French, SUD; 'flowing backwards' turns it to DUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is the great river of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Free ball produces clearance

parts.note: to free is to rid
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A complimentary dance results in something being cleared away.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something, a clearing out.

clue.text: Equipped with a sort of crude coat

indicators.note: sort of hints the letters are sorted into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitted out in a rough garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutred means dressed or fitted out with gear.

clue.text: One's concern being the yield perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: Interest is what one is involved in, a stake or concern, and also the return paid on money lent.

clue.text: Elegant newcomer to broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young newcomer to society
being broadcast is being on air

explanation.surface: A stylish recruit joins the radio or TV world.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and stylish in manner.

clue.text: Part of service record is let out

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: out shows the following words are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A section of a church service is recorded, and someone lets it be released.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle is the reading from an apostle's letter in the Communion service.

clue.text: Cesario's building at Olivia's gate?

parts.note: In Twelfth Night Viola, disguised as Cesario, says she would make a willow shelter at Olivia's gate

explanation.walkthrough: The line from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night is 'Make me a willow cabin at your gate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small hut or shelter, the kind of dwelling Viola imagines building.

clue.text: A bold front supplies support against trouble

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
V, versus, means against
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A display of courage provides backing in the face of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness intended to impress or hide fear.

clue.text: Religious leader marries Jack to Elizabeth

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A cleric weds a sailor to a woman named Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marries' and 'to' just join the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a community of nuns.

clue.text: Soldiers ordered to carry gear

indicators.note: to carry means the commanded word holds the equipment inside

parts.note: bade is past tense of bid, meaning ordered
a rig is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Troops are commanded to transport their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an adjective on soldiers but is the past tense of bid, giving BADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions of troops.

clue.text: Stand by for a pound, say, for — instance

indicators.note: say signals the measure word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a pound, for instance, is a weight

explanation.surface: Wait for a pound coin, say, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for instance' tells us the pound is an example of a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To await is to wait for, to stand by expecting something.

clue.text: Bring up point repeatedly about money

indicators.note: about means the doubled compass point surrounds the coin
repeatedly means the point is used twice

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
a ducat is an old gold coin, money

explanation.surface: Someone raises a matter again and again concerning cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives E twice, and 'about' wraps those around DUCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to rear and teach it, to school it.

clue.text: Run over

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run scored not off the bat, an extra; extra also means over and above.

clue.text: Befuddle and confuse Irene a bit

indicators.note: confuse means the letters of these words are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to bewilder and muddle a woman called Irene slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate is to make drunk, fuddling the senses.

clue.text: Of different shades of meaning

parts.note: shades means both colours of the rainbow and ghosts, so the word relates to both senses

explanation.definitionFit: Spectral describes a spectrum of colours and also something ghostly, a shade being a phantom.

clue.text: Accomplished by a doctor, there's nothing to it

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic does a job and declares it simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and dexterous, as an accomplished performer is.
